content:
Key observations from the test image:
- Close-up of a soybean stem at a node
- **Gray/grayish-white fluffy fungal growth** at the node junction
- Surrounding leaves are yellow/senescing
- Stem itself appears green

The gray fluffy growth at the node strongly points to **White_Mold** or possibly **Diaporthe**. Let me check references.

White Mold reference shows fluffy white/gray mycelial growth at stem nodes — very similar to the test image. Diaporthe shows darker stem lesions and black pycnidia — doesn't match.

Let me check a couple more candidates to be thorough.

Anthracnose shows dark brown stems with scattered black fruiting bodies. Phomopsis shows pod discoloration with pycnidia. Neither matches the gray fluffy node growth in the test image.

**Initial prediction: White_Mold** — the gray fluffy mycelial growth at the stem node is the hallmark symptom.

Now checking the Attractor Guide.
White_Mold is over-predicted. Must check Phomopsis (4x), Tobacco_Streak_Virus (2x), Charcoal_Rot (1x). Already viewed Phomopsis — pods/seeds, not matching. Checking the others.

Tobacco_Streak_Virus shows pod/seed discoloration and plant proliferation — no fluffy stem growth. Charcoal_Rot shows bleached/dried gray stems with internal discoloration — no fluffy mycelium at nodes.

None of the alternatives match the test image. The gray fluffy mycelial growth at the stem node is definitively White_Mold (Sclerotinia sclerotiorum).

The White_Mold reference collage shows identical fluffy fungal growth at stem nodes. Alternatives from the attractor guide (Phomopsis, Tobacco_Streak_Virus, Charcoal_Rot, Diaporthe) all show distinct symptoms — pod/seed discoloration, bleached dry stems, or black pycnidia in rows — none of which match the fluffy node growth visible here."}
